column2: Why are baseline function and speed of change treated as diagnostic vital signs in older people?
column3: Narrowed reserve lets acute illness cross several thresholds at once, so it presents as a fall, confusion, immobility, poor intake, or new dependence rather than a textbook organ syndrome.

column3: In neurogenic hypotension the heart-rate rise is disproportionately small for the pressure fall; in volume depletion it is greater than usual, though beta blockers and a pacemaker alter interpretation.
